subject: Hosted API commit uptick — ops playbook, surge pocket & rate fencing
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@picocart.com>; Tom Whitman <t.whitman@picocart.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API commit uptick — ops playbook, surge pocket & rate fencing

Hi Elena / Tom,

Great conversation this morning — appreciate you walking through PicoCart's projected Black Friday traffic. As discussed, we can support the Q4 burst with a temporary commit uplift plus a dedicated surge pocket to avoid throttle risk. Attached is a concise playbook (Commit_Summary_Q4.xlsx) and a redlined order form (PicoCart_OrderForm_v3.pdf) that reflects: 

- Monthly committed tokens increase from 6M -> 12M (3-month uplift window: Oct–Dec)
- Surge pocket: 2M tokens available for on-demand use at the negotiated overage rate
- Soft throttle thresholds and a hard failover policy to a lower-cost model if token latency tolerances are exceeded

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review the order form and playbook; flag any procurement/legal asks
2) If procurement is comfortable, sign PO/DD and we send DocuSign for the amendment
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min ops handoff with our infra lead to map caching/batching settings for your peak windows

I’ve cc'd Vanessa for billing/pricing confirmation and Lauren for the handshake on rollout/CS.

Attachments: PicoCart_OrderForm_v3.pdf (PDF, 180KB), Commit_Summary_Q4.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@picocart.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Whitman <t.whitman@picocart.com>, procurement@picocart.com
Date: 2026-09-15T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uptick — ops playbook, surge pocket & rate fencing

Thanks Sergio — the materials look clear. A couple of questions before we move to legal/procurement: 

- Can the surge pocket be consumed without triggering a higher overage multiplier if we stay within the 2M cap? We need predictable unit economics for the 48-hour peak window.
- For the soft throttle you mentioned, can we get a service-level guarantee for median p50 latency under peak conditions? We may need a short SLA clause for the three-week period in November.

Procurement also asked for your SOC2 report to complete our vendor checklist — can you attach that?

If we can get clarity on those three points, I’ll push to get purchase approval next week.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Engineering, PicoCart
elena.morales@picocart.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@picocart.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uptick — ops playbook, surge pocket & rate fencing

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick review. Quick answers: 

- Surge pocket behavior: yes, the 2M surge pocket is treated as a separate bucket billed at the agreed overage rate (no multiplier), provided it does not exceed the pocket in a single 30-day billing period. We can add a clause in the order form that explicitly calls out the 48-hour peak exemption for calculation purposes.

- Latency: For the temporary uplift window we can offer a p50 latency target for text-generation endpoints of <= 180ms across our US-hosted nodes. We can commit to an operational response time (investigation) SLA of 4 hours for any degradation during the peak period. We cannot extend a monetary uptime SLA for a short-term uplift, but we will include a rollback/fallback plan to a verified smaller model if latency exceeds the target for two consecutive 10-min windows.

- SOC2: attaching the latest report.

Attachment: SOC2-report-2025.pdf (PDF, 620KB)

I’ll loop in Karthik to confirm billing/pricing language to add to the doc.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: procurement@picocart.com; Elena Morales <elena.morales@picocart.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uptick — ops playbook, surge pocket & rate fencing

Hi Elena / procurement team —

Following Vanessa's note, a couple of drafting clarifications for the order form: 

- Billing cadence: commit charges will be invoiced monthly in arrears. The 2M surge pocket will be shown as a separate line item and will only be invoiced when consumed.
- Overages: standard overage rate is $0.0008/token. For this uplift window we are offering a temporary capped overage of $0.0006/token applied exclusively to the surge pocket.
- Soft throttle: we will include operational thresholds and a defined rollback trigger; penalties are limited to service credits capped at one month of committed fees (we can discuss escalations but procurement asked we keep this simple).

If procurement needs specific language for PO creation (billing address, remit-to), please send the PO template and we’ll populate it.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Contracts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Tom Whitman <t.whitman@picocart.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@picocart.com>, procurement@picocart.com
Date: 2026-09-20T14:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uptick — ops playbook, surge pocket & rate fencing

Sergio / Karthik — good summary. Procurement is comfortable with the pricing but wants a small tweak: can the surge pocket billing be prorated if we use less than 2M tokens across the three-month uplift window? We'd prefer pay-for-what-you-use rather than a full bucket charge.

Also legal wants the rollback/fallback to be tested during a pre-peak dry run — can we schedule an ops-run on Oct 18 (30–45 min) to validate the fallback model and routing?

If those two items are acceptable we’ll get an internal sign-off and issue a PO by Oct 1.

Thanks,
Tom Whitman
VP Product | PicoCart LLC
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tom Whitman <t.whitman@picocart.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@picocart.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uptick — ops playbook, surge pocket & rate fencing

Tom / Elena — happy to confirm both asks: 

- Proration: we can bill the surge pocket only for the tokens consumed. The order form will show the 2M as the maximum available and actual invoiced usage will be prorated per billing period.
- Ops dry run: Oct 18 at 10:00am PT works for our infra/ops team. We’ll run through the fallback to the smaller model, validate KV cache warmup, and check the billing metrics emitted to your telemetry. Expect a calendar invite from me shortly.

I’ll also update the order form to reflect these points and re-share the DocuSign link once procurement confirms final PO fields.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@picocart.com>, Tom Whitman <t.whitman@picocart.com>, procurement@picocart.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-24T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uptick — ops playbook, surge pocket & rate fencing

Team — great progress. Updated order form attached; highlights:
- 6M -> 12M monthly commit (Oct–Dec), surge pocket max 2M tokens, billed only for usage, capped overage rate $0.0006/token.
- p50 latency target <= 180ms for text-generation endpoints; rollback triggers and an Oct 18 dry run confirmed.
- SOC2 attached for procurement.

If Picocart approves the PO, we’ll issue the DocuSign today and target provisioning on Oct 5 so platform tuning and cache priming can happen ahead of the dry run.

Attachments: PicoCart_OrderForm_v3.pdf (updated), Commit_Summary_Q4.xlsx

Sergio
